name: watering hole by speed
description: Win by getting one of your animals onto the water hole at d4, the middle square, with none of the animals that eat it beside it; faster animals move first. Almost every game is won at the hole, though eating all of the other side's animals wins too. Each round both players choose a move in secret, then the two moves are made one after the other, the faster animal's first and the slower one on the board the first one left, if it still can be. Cats are the fastest, then rats, then dogs, then elephants. No two kinds share a speed, so two moves never collide, and who moves first is decided each round by which animals the two players chose to move; when both sides step onto the hole in one round, the faster animal gets there first and wins on the spot if nothing that eats it is beside it. White's elephants and cats face Black's dogs and rats on a 7x7 board, every animal stepping one square in any direction, and each kind eats exactly one enemy kind: elephant eats dog, dog eats cat, cat eats rat, rat eats elephant. Speed cuts across that chain. A cat is faster than the rat it hunts and a rat faster than the elephant it hunts, so those hunters catch their prey where it stands, before it can run. An elephant is slower than the dog it hunts and a dog slower than the cat, so that prey always escapes a strike by moving away, and its slow hunter catches it only when it stays put, or when it steps onto the very square the hunter was moving to, arriving first and being eaten there.

provenance.preview: A preview: a new kind of game played in rounds in which faster pieces move first, still being tested. Play it against the computer for practice; it is on no leaderboard yet, and its score is a first reading, not yet trusted.
provenance.source: docs/archive/plan-speed.md, Q943c: the showcases of schema 28's speed (section 6.1)
provenance.history: T3 of docs/archive/plan-speed.md section 6.1, pre-registered 2026-10-16 before it was built: the watering hole (5c0b017473f5) with the cat at speed 3, the rat 2, the dog 1 and the elephant 0, and rules.simultaneous.tie impossible removed (inert where no two opposing kinds share a speed, section 4.1). The game designed around the rule: strictly ordered, so no round collides, swaps or is void, and each side has one hunter faster than its prey and one slower. Built by Q943c (2026-10-19); measured and graded against section 6.3 by Q943d. Joined the library from preview by Q943f (2026-10-19): the library's only game in which pieces have speeds (schema 28's pieces[].speed), so every round is two moves made in order, the faster first, and nothing collides; speed cuts across the watering hole's food chain, two hunters catching their prey where it stands and two catching it only standing still, and two arrivals at the hole are a race rather than a meeting. Viable in 3 of 4 runs at 0.557, every game decided at the hole with the seat level. Returned to the previews by Q996 (2026-10-21, docs/reference/library-repair-2026-10-21.md): with the round player that sees a finished round's value (Q986b) it measured 0.395, not viable 0-4, its games over in about five rounds (the quick-kill gate in three runs, a seat refusal in one); a guard that a faster hunter is beside cannot run, so the ring of guards that makes the hole a contest falls in two or three rounds, and no starting layout tried (five) kept the idea and made a longer game.
